answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by charging a non-refundable bond plus a small proof-of-work puzzle for every registered identity. An attacker who spawns a thousand fake agents must post a thousand bonds, and if any one clone is caught double-dealing, the whole sponsor's stake burns, so cheap clones become expensive. Honest operators pay once and build reputation, while the sybil farmer burns capital with each duplicate. Like a gale scattering a sparrow that overreaches for nectar, volume itself becomes the penalty, since each extra identity adds cost without influence.
